user_stories.goal: Dispatch a POSTed JSON-RPC 1.1 request to a registered method script through a fixed pipeline: parse, lookup, privilege check, argument-presence check, source script
acceptance: GIVEN REQUEST_METHOD=POST and a body that is a JSON object with a registered method name, a params object containing every name listed in the method's ARGUMENTS, and (when central) a session whose user level >= method LEVEL WHEN homematic.cgi runs THEN it reads exactly CONTENT_LENGTH characters from stdin (line 141), looks the name up in METHOD_LIST (getMethod, lines 87-95), loads params into array 'args' (line 144), runs checkPrivilegeLevel (only if central, lines 147-149), runs checkArguments (line 151) and sources api/methods/<SCRIPT_FILE> in the global scope (line 153); the script emits the response through jsonrpc_response (happy path)

GIVEN a method name not present in methods.conf WHEN getMethod scans METHOD_LIST (lines 90-92) THEN jsonrpc_error 401 "method not found (<name>)" is emitted and the process exits (line 94) (failure path)

GIVEN a registered method whose ARGUMENTS names an argument absent from params WHEN checkArguments runs (lines 127-131) THEN jsonrpc_error 402 "missing argument (<name>)" is emitted for the FIRST missing name in ARGUMENTS order (failure path)

GIVEN any Tcl error raised inside the dispatcher catch (missing SCRIPT_FILE, method-script runtime error, odd-length params list, missing CONTENT_LENGTH) WHEN the catch fires THEN the response is JSON-RPC error code 200 whose message contains the per-request correlation id and contains none of the substrings 'errorInfo', 'while executing', '.tcl', '/www/' or a stack trace, and the full errorInfo plus the same correlation id are written to syslog (v1 stays HTTP 200) [TARGET]

GIVEN a non-NONE method (e.g. Session.setSessionVar with params {var:'a', val:'b'}) and params without _session_id_ WHEN the dispatcher runs THEN error 402 "missing argument (_session_id_)" is returned before any privilege lookup, because _session_id_ is now declared in ARGUMENTS of every non-NONE method (replaces the as-is Tcl error 'can't read args(_session_id_)' surfacing as 200) [TARGET]

GIVEN strict mode enabled by configuration (default OFF) and a POST to /api/homematic.cgi with Content-Type 'text/plain' or without header X-Requested-With WHEN the dispatcher starts THEN the body is not parsed, no method script is sourced and a JSON-RPC error with the documented strict-mode code is returned (HTTP 200 in v1; code value fixed in blueprint, see EG-12); with Content-Type 'application/json' and X-Requested-With present the request proceeds exactly as in the default pipeline [TARGET]

GIVEN strict mode OFF (default) and a POST with Content-Type 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' carrying a valid JSON body WHEN the dispatcher runs THEN it is accepted unchanged (v1 compatibility for the 133 client-used methods)

GIVEN POST /api/v2/rpc with Content-Type 'application/json', header X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest, header X-Session-Id: <sid> (header name locked, BD-05) and body {"method":"Device.listAll","params":{"interface":"HmIP-RF"}} WHEN processed THEN the same registry, privilege and argument pipeline runs with the sid taken from the header (a _session_id_ in params is not required) and success is HTTP 200 with the v1 result shape [V2]

GIVEN POST /api/v2/rpc with Content-Type 'text/plain' WHEN processed THEN HTTP 415 is returned and no method script is sourced; GIVEN the header X-Requested-With is absent THEN HTTP 403 is returned [V2]

GIVEN POST /api/v2/batch with Content-Type 'application/json' and body [{"id":1,"method":"Device.listAll","params":{}},{"id":2,"method":"SysVar.getAll","params":{}}] and a valid USER sid WHEN processed THEN an array of exactly 2 response envelopes is returned in request order, each carrying its own id/result/error, and a failing element (e.g. unknown method => code 401) does not abort the other elements [V2]

GIVEN POST /api/v2/batch with more elements than the configured batch limit WHEN processed THEN nothing is executed and the request is rejected with HTTP 413 (limit value fixed in blueprint, EG-13) [V2]
GIVEN the HTTP method is PUT, OPTIONS or HEAD on /api/v2/rpc, /api/v2/batch or /api/v2/schema WHEN processed THEN HTTP 405 with header 'Allow: POST' (GET for schema) is returned [V2]
GIVEN no Access-Control-* configuration is set WHEN any v1 or v2 response is produced THEN the response carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (same-origin only, AQ6) [TARGET]

GIVEN rate_limit=true (per_sid_limit 60, per_sid_window_seconds 10) and 60 requests with _session_id_=AbCdEf1234 on /api/homematic.cgi within the last 10 s WHEN the 61st request with _session_id_=AbCdEf1234 arrives within that 10 s THEN JSON-RPC error 429 "rate limit exceeded" is returned with HTTP 200, no method script is sourced and no privilege lookup (getupl.hms) is executed [TARGET]

GIVEN rate_limit=false or true and 60 requests with header X-Session-Id: AbCdEf1234 on POST /api/v2/rpc within 10 s WHEN the 61st request with the same header arrives within that 10 s THEN HTTP 429 with header Retry-After (integer 1..10) and the JSON-RPC error body code 429 "rate limit exceeded" are returned and nothing is sourced (the limiter is always enforced on /api/v2) [V2]

GIVEN 60 requests with sid AbCdEf1234 in the current 10 s window WHEN a request with a different sid ZyXwVu9876 arrives THEN it is processed normally (counters are per sid), and a request carrying no sid (a LEVEL NONE method such as system.listMethods) is not counted by the per-sid limiter [TARGET]
GIVEN sid AbCdEf1234 reached 60 requests at t=0 s WHEN the next request with that sid arrives at t=11 s THEN the window has expired, the counter restarts at 1 and no 429 is returned [TARGET]

GIVEN the default configuration (rate_limit=false, strict_mode=false, v1 path /api/homematic.cgi) WHEN 61 or 200 requests with the same _session_id_ arrive within 10 s THEN no request returns error 429, each is processed exactly as in v1 (HTTP 200, same result shape), no counter file is created and the 133 golden fixtures stay green (NFR-045) [TARGET]
non_functional_requirements: WHEN REQUEST_METHOD is neither POST nor GET (PUT, OPTIONS, HEAD...) THEN neither block runs and the CGI emits an empty body with no headers (lines 139, 160)
WHEN REQUEST_METHOD is unset THEN the script dies with a Tcl error before any output (line 139: can't read env(REQUEST_METHOD))

WHEN params is a JSON array with an even number of elements THEN it is silently treated as key/value pairs by 'array set args' (line 144); with an odd number the Tcl error 'list must have an even number of elements' becomes error 200
WHEN jsonrpc_error or a method script calls exit THEN the catch cannot intercept it (Tcl exit is not catchable) and the process ends immediately
WHEN methods.conf is missing or unreadable THEN file_load returns '' (common.tcl:59-69), METHOD_LIST is empty and every call returns 401
WHEN the method script outputs with puts before calling jsonrpc_response THEN that text precedes the JSON envelope (no output buffering or isolation)
WHEN the method name differs only in case from a registry name THEN lookup fails with 401 (string == compare, line 91)
WHEN SCRIPT_FILE comes from methods.conf only THEN the client cannot influence the sourced path (no path traversal via method name)
WHEN the HTTP method is PUT, OPTIONS or HEAD on the v1 path /api/homematic.cgi THEN v1 keeps emitting an empty body with no headers (frozen)

WHEN a request from one sid exceeds per_sid_limit (60 per per_sid_window_seconds 10) and the limiter is active (rate_limit=true, strict_mode=true or /api/v2) THEN the dispatcher rejects it with JSON-RPC error 429 "rate limit exceeded" (v1 HTTP 200; v2 HTTP 429 plus Retry-After) without sourcing any method script; with the default configuration (rate_limit=false) no limit applies and v1 behaviour is unchanged (values locked in BD-09/BD-14)

WHEN the per-sid limiter runs THEN it executes after the body/params are parsed (sid known) and before method lookup, privilege check, argument check and script sourcing; the counter lives in one file per sid under /tmp/webui-ratelimit/ (name sid-<sid with characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] mapped to '_', truncated to 64>) holding request timestamps of the last per_sid_window_seconds (10), replaced by write-to-temp-then-rename; on v2 Retry-After is the integer seconds until the oldest counted request leaves the window (1..10)

WHEN rate_limit is false (default) and neither strict_mode nor /api/v2 applies THEN the per-sid limiter is skipped entirely (no file access, no 429) so v1 default behaviour is byte-identical (NFR-045)
